sections.content: How many people are "estimators, valuers and assessors"?

44,985 people

were counted on the census as "estimators, valuers and assessors" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Estimators, valuers and assessors calculate the probable costs of various kinds of projects, estimate the value of property (both buildings and items), and investigate insurance claims to assess their validity and to assign liability.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "estimators, valuers and assessors" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "estimators, valuers and assessors", 12.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "estimators, valuers and assessors" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "estimators, valuers and assessors" included:

  • routine inspectors and testers
  • electrical and electronic trades (other)
  • electronics engineers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "estimators, valuers and assessors" there were more men than women (70.9% compared with 29.1%).

This means "estimators, valuers and assessors" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 70.9% and women made up 29.1% of "estimators, valuers and assessors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "estimators, valuers and assessors" included:

  • photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators
  • clergy
  • upholsterers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "estimators, valuers and assessors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "estimators, valuers and assessors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "estimators, valuers and assessors", 8.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (85.7% compared with 14.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (90.3%) than self-employed (9.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
